_open_questions: DSP compute budget: with up to 60 bands stacked (30 virtual-channel + 30 output) plus crossover + phase + delay, is there a practical ceiling before the 2x295MHz DSP saturates?

Whether the three tiers listed here (virtual channels, physical outputs, inputs) are ALL the tiers this DSP exposes is UNKNOWN. `groups_enumerated: false` is what says so to a machine; this line says why. It stood at `true` from 2026-08-23 until 2026-08-31, and that was an error of the same kind this file elsewhere warns about: the owner named the input tier when asked, and STOPPED LISTING -- which is not the same statement as `that is all of them`. `true` makes the absence of a group a POSITIVE CLAIM that the DSP lacks that tier (see `rew_tool/dsp_profile.py`), so the profile was asserting on his behalf something he had not said. Corrected on his ruling, 2026-08-31: `I did not say that`, and not knowing is itself an answer -- it means false.

Delay quantiser: rounding or truncation upward? Both fractional values measured on 2026-09-02 (4.800 and 30.720 samples) sat ABOVE the half-sample, so the data cannot tell. One electrical capture at a delay whose fraction sits below the half-sample (e.g. 0.03 ms = 2.880 samples at 96 kHz) decides it. Costs at most half a sample (5.2 us) either way; worth knowing before any sheet snaps to the grid (docs/TODO.md S-002)

Phase control step on mid/high channels: 5.625 deg is measured on a SUBWOOFER channel; the mid/high block captured only 180 deg, which sits on a 5.625 grid and an 11.25 one alike, and older PC-Tool generations are reported to step mid/high by 11.25. One capture of one step on a mid/high channel at a reference below 1 kHz decides it (bench series 3, 2026-09-02)

channel_gain.note: the same range on both tiers (user, PC-Tool, 2026-08-23). Deliberately NOT the EQ band's -30..+12: they are different controls and the asymmetry is the proof. Step 1.0 dB (user, PC-Tool on his own unit, 2026-08-23) — note it is COARSER than the EQ band's 0.1 dB, another reason the two must not stand in for each other.

delay.note: the ceiling is per tier AND the two tiers SUM -- enter a delay in one layer only, keep the other at 0 (user, PC-Tool, 2026-07-15).
delay.sample_quantised_note: a typed delay is quantised to a WHOLE SAMPLE at the processing rate -- 10.4167 us at 96 kHz (bench 2026-09-02, fact 3, read off the phase slope of each ratio with 0.13 deg residual): 0.05 ms = 4.800 samples lands on 5.0003, 0.32 ms = 30.720 on 30.9996, 1.00 ms = 96.000 on 95.9981. The published step '3.5 mm or 0.01 ms' is that figure rounded, and a model built on 0.01 ms drifts 4 % -- about 0.4 mm per 10 mm of claimed alignment. `step_ms` stays the UI's ENTRY step; what the device HOLDS is the whole-sample count, which is the samples column of the settings sheet (state/apply.py). Both fractional values measured sat above the half-sample, so rounding and truncation upward are not separated by this data (see _open_questions)

dsp_profile.dsp_processing_rate_note: the PROCESSING rate the DSP runs at -- delays in samples derive from it. NOT the capture rate: what a measurement was recorded at is a separate fact that lives with the measurement (a UMIK-1 capturing at 48k under this 96k DSP is legitimate; warn once, work with it). Renamed from sample_rate_hz 2026-08-25; the old name is still read

crossover_filters.corner_freq_note: 20-20480 Hz on EVERY channel, the sub included (user, PC-Tool, 2026-08-23). The sub channel's UI OFFERS 20-300, and higher can still be entered by hand -- so 300 is advisory, not a bound, and must not be written as one: refusing a legitimate sub crossover above 300 Hz is the same class of error as silently rounding LR48 to LR36, inverted.

CHEBYSHEV.ripple_db_note: MEASURED AND NOT IDENTIFIED — deferred permanently, not merely unasked. An experiment was run and could not identify the mathematics (user, 2026-08-23), so this is a closed line of enquiry rather than a lookup nobody has done: do not re-ask, and do not expect a cheap retry. The consequence is bigger than one null: with the ripple unidentified the filter is not DETERMINED, so a Chebyshev crossover on this processor can be entered and cannot be modelled, predicted or checked against a target. `dsp_math.XO_OPTIONS` already excludes the family from any search for that reason; `resonalyze_vc` reports such an edge as unverifiable rather than passing it. Also do not read the 6-42 dB/oct beside it into this field — that answer was about the SLOPE ladder and shares only a conversation with this question.

crossover_filters.verification_note: VERIFIED AGAINST THE HARDWARE (electrical bench 2026-08-31 .. 2026-09-04; ayukhno/autosound-measurements, hardware/helix/dsp-ultra-s, fact 8 and 9): LR12, LR24, LR36, BW24, BW42 and BE36 are bilinear-transformed DIGITAL biquad chains at the processing rate, LR(n) = BW(n/2) squared, Bessel normalised at -3 dB (dsp_math's norm='mag'), and the chain is a plain product of sections (HP 500 x LP 5000 measured separately and multiplied match both engaged to 0.015 dB / 0.11 deg). dsp_math.xo_response against eight published curves: 0.04-0.09 dB and 0.19-0.48 deg rms on the files' own 1/96-octave grid, band and mask stated per case. BW24 at 460 Hz -- the question of hub #32 -- sits -0.0024 dB / +0.034 deg from the LR24 control captured in the same 54-second pass and reads -2.985 dB at its corner; at 8 kHz the analogue prototype is refused by the hardware where the digital form fits, which is the measurement behind binding the model to dsp_processing_rate_hz. Polarity follows the alignment: LR12 and LR36 need one leg inverted, LR24 and BW42 do not. Fixtures and the exact windows: rew_tool/testdata/helix-bench/ (dsp_math selftest). CHEBYSHEV stays as below: enterable, not modellable

groups.label: Input stage (high-level) — OUT OF METHOD SCOPE
groups.note: The stage EXISTS on this processor, and it is NOT a tuning tier like the other two. Its job is forming the INPUT signal when the source is a factory head unit's speaker-level outputs. On optical, Bluetooth or USB it is not in the path at all (user, 2026-08-23). OUT OF SCOPE for this method, deliberately and not for now: undoing what a factory head unit already did — its EQ, its delays, its all-passes — to recover a flat input is a different problem from tuning a system, and this method does not solve it. So expect NO ledger rows for this tier, and do not read its absence from a ledger as an incomplete project. Recorded rather than deleted because the hardware fact is true and belongs in a MODEL profile; what is scoped out is our work on it, not its existence.

dsp_profile.name: Helix DSP Ultra S

parametric_eq.gain_note: the EQ BAND's gain. Step 0.1 dB, corroborated on the same 2026-08-23 panel (Gain 0.1 dB). The channel trim is `channel_gain` below, and the two are now measured as different in all three of range (-30..+12 against -30..+5), step (0.1 against 1.0) and resolution — from his own screen, so 'they must never stand in for each other' is a measurement rather than a caution.
parametric_eq.mode_note: OBSERVED, not derived, 2026-08-23. The PC-Tool panel whose selector reads 'Parametric EQ' was photographed in ONE state with every field visible at once: Freq 26.01 Hz, Gain 0.1 dB, Q 50. So the frequency field ACCEPTS two decimals (not merely displays them — that was the open reservation) and Q reaches 50 in that same panel. The pair recorded here therefore co-occurs in a single mode, and the union stops being an inference. Fine EQ pairs a 1 Hz step with Q 0.5-15; this panel is the other one. PROVENANCE: this supersedes the DERIVED label required while the pair was unobserved — that requirement was SATISFIED, not dropped, and the distinction matters because a requirement quietly abandoned looks identical afterwards to one that was met. What the panel does NOT establish, so it does not travel with this: the BOTTOM of the Q range (0.5 is recorded from elsewhere; nothing here shows it), and whether some third mode has different limits again — which no longer matters, since the question was only whether this pair exists in one mode.
parametric_eq.q_note: What the METHOD should use is narrower still than what the hardware takes, and that is not a hardware question -- see the spatial-validity Q ceiling in the method's diagnostic reference.
parametric_eq.q_range_by_type_note: MEASURED on the bench of 2026-09-01 (20 electrical sweeps, hub #36 / RES-002): PC-Tool accepts a SHELF's Q only within 0.3 .. 2, while the bell reaches the 50 recorded in `q_range`. One range for every type was wrong in both directions -- it called a legitimate shelf at Q 0.3 out of range, and passed a shelf at Q 30 that the processor will not take. `resonalyze_vc` reads this override for the types named here and falls back to `q_range` for the rest. The same bench also settled that the Q typed into a Helix shelf IS the RBJ Q: a free fit of the measurement returned 0.300 / 0.707 / 1.998 for the three entered values, residual 0.005 dB.
parametric_eq.shelf_note: PC-Tool's LS_Q/HS_Q at Q=0.7071 is identical to an RBJ shelf at S=1 (0.000 dB), so model them in REW with its 'LS Q'/'HS Q' types -- REW's plain 'Low shelf'/'High shelf' is a different definition and will not match. Note also that shelf Q is NEVER rescaled between PEQ Q conventions (a shelf Q sets a knee, not a bandwidth): anything converting Q for a non-RBJ target must skip shelves or it silently widens every one of them.

phase_control.corner_ceiling_note: 3/16 of the rate. Measured ONLY at 96 kHz: three recoveries at two references gave 18007-18010 Hz, which is 3/16 of the rate AND an absolute 18 kHz to within the spread -- one rate cannot separate them. The rate-relative reading is the one taken (Resonalyze's too: the corner is placed in the digital domain); on a 48 kHz unit the two differ, and this is the field to correct if one is ever measured. Whether the ceiling is deliberate or a firmware defect is not established; the manufacturer documents neither it nor its consequences. Positions lost to it: 0 below a 1001 Hz reference (the documented grid works exactly), 2 at 2000, 3 at 3000, 5 at 5000, 9 at 8000 -- arithmetic from the ceiling and the step (phase_rotation.lost_settings)
phase_control.cost_note: not a polarity flip: 180 deg at a 5 kHz reference is -23 deg at 1 kHz. Not free: the group delay of the realized section is a plateau BELOW the corner, a peak at it and a fall away above -- 270 deg at a 5 kHz reference costs 102 us over 20-500 Hz; 180 deg at a 500 Hz reference costs 640-690 us over 20-100 Hz (about 22 cm of path) and 1.27 ms at the corner. The cost lands in the sub/midbass joint the control is usually used to fix (phase_rotation.group_delay_us)
phase_control.implementation: one RBJ second-order all-pass with Q = 1.0000, whose corner the processor places so that the filter's phase equals the setting AT the channel's reference crossover -- capped at corner_ceiling_fraction_of_rate x the processing rate (18 kHz at 96 kHz); above that, settings collapse onto one filter and deliver an angle that is not on the grid. MEASURED on the bench of 2026-09-01/02 (~60 electrical sweeps; ayukhno/autosound-measurements, hardware/helix/dsp-ultra-s, fact 6, CC BY 4.0), implemented upstream in DIMOSUS/Resonalyze dsp/PhaseRotationControl.cs @ bc957c8 and verified there on all 32 published cases (median phase residual 0.19 deg rms, median corner agreement 0.10 %); ported as rew_tool/phase_rotation.py and applied by predict.py to any ledger row carrying phase_deg beside its crossover. The method's reading: references/tooling/helix-phase-allpass.md
phase_control.present_on_roles_note: per Audiotec-Fischer: subwoofer channels and the mid/high channels of a fully active system; `fullrange` and `low` channels get plain 0/180 polarity instead. A hardware statement about channel TYPE -- distinct from the method's rule that the midbass is the anchor one does not rotate; both stand
phase_control.reference: configured LPF on a sub channel, configured HPF otherwise
phase_control.reference_note: AS CONFIGURED, not as active: Bypass and slope = OFF leave the reference in place (three states measured, 0.018 dB and 0.12 deg apart). Reading the LIVE crossover gives the wrong corner on every channel whose filter is switched off. In the ledger a switched-off but configured crossover is written with its f and slope OFF, which predict keeps out of the chain and still reads as the reference (predict._phase_reference). A row with an angle and no configured reference is refused by name: the angle is stated AT a crossover, so without one it is not a filter
phase_control.scope: per driver output. The virtual tier declares the field too (groups[].fields) and was not measured there
phase_control.step_note: 360/64; a full 360 is not offered. MEASURED on a subwoofer channel (one step -5.54 deg against a nominal 5.625, two steps -11.29 against 11.25, at a 500 Hz reference). The mid/high block only captured 180 deg, which sits on a 5.625 grid and an 11.25 one alike, and older PC-Tool generations are reported to step mid/high by 11.25 -- so the step is measured for one channel type and ASSUMED for the others (see _open_questions)

polarity.note: double-inversion possible (driver stage + virtual channel stage); net effect cancels if both are inverted
